s: Tseerutsaydan, a proud king, worships seventy idols and forces his people to sacrifice to them. The book warns that those who worship idols will be punished.
Maqabis of the tribe of Benjamin has three strong sons who refuse to bow to the king's idols. They are put to death, and rise again shining brighter than the sun.
A voice from heaven calls the martyrs Abya, Sila and Fentos. They are given to wild beasts and fire, but they do not fear, and angels carry their souls to Paradise.
Fire cannot burn the martyrs' bodies, the sea will not drown them and the beasts will not touch them. The five martyrs appear to the king by night and tell him that God alone is to be worshipped.
Proud kings like Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar were humbled. God alone led Israel, and he hears those who pray to him.
God gives kingdoms to those who do his will, and he will repay the kings who despise his word, as he repaid Saul.
A king is only a creature: as he rules his servants, God rules him and will judge him by his deeds.
The resurrection of the dead: as God brings fruit from the vine and life from the tree, he will raise the dead with the dew of life.
As the land needs rain to grow green, so the dead need God's mercy to rise. All flesh will rise again.
The patriarchs wanted to be buried with their fathers so as to rise together with them. God, who gives life, is able to raise the dead.
Judgment on Tyre, Sidon and the idolaters, whose vine is the vine of Sodom.
Jerusalem is rebuked for sinning like Sodom and Gomorrah. God will repay those who forsake him and honour those who keep his word.
God foretells a proud man of destruction. The fall of Satan and his angels, who did not praise their Creator in humility.
God cleansed the earth with the flood. He made a covenant with Noah, freed Israel from Egypt and fed them, but they made the golden calf and were punished.
Akrandyos, king of Midian, attacks Israel. Brave men give their lives for the people.
The nations in their lands: some do good and know God, others do evil and will be judged. Praise of Jerusalem, God's holy city.
The armies of Edom and Amalek, who do not fear God, and the sins Satan teaches them.
Remember that you will stand before God. The giants and the angels who sinned brought death, while the righteous fathers lived long.
The sons of Cain invented music and pleasures, and through them the fallen angels led mankind astray. God hears the prayer of those who keep his law.
God protects and rewards those who do good and saves them from their enemies.
David trusted in God and was saved from all his enemies. Wicked kings who did not trust in him were not saved.
Remember the names of the good kings and imitate them. Defend the orphan and the widow.
Do not walk in the way of Cain, who killed his meek brother out of jealousy. God loves the meek, like Abel.
Gideon won with a small army because he trusted in God. God asks why his people serve other gods after all he has done for them.
The wicked follow Satan's crooked way and will be repaid. God rules the world and feeds all creatures.
God is just: he gives the poor and the righteous their reward and shows no partiality to rich or poor.
God created the world in six days and made Adam in his image. After his sin, Adam was sent out to work the earth in sweat and sorrow.
Adam's children, good and evil. Cain kills Abel. Israel's history of sin, oppression and rescue by the judges.
God sent Moses and Aaron to free Israel from Egypt. He rejected Saul and chose David to be king.
God rejected the house of Saul for disobedience. He loves those who love him and feeds all creatures.
Kings rule only by God's will. He gave David favour and Solomon wisdom, and saved David from all his enemies.
Kings and princes are told to keep God's commands and not grieve him as Israel did.
God fed Israel with manna, but they did not worship him. Man is mortal and should not boast.
A prophecy of the rise and fall of kingdoms, and of the testing of all people at the last day.
Woes on the mighty of Israel who neglect the orphan and the widow and live in drunkenness. A sinful land will be laid waste.
Warnings to the proud nations. Israel's ingratitude in the desert. At the resurrection the righteous will reign with God for ever.
i: The three books of Meqabyan are found only in the Bible of the Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox Churches. Despite the name, they are not the books of Maccabees in the Catholic Bible and do not tell the story of Judas Maccabeus. They were written in Ge’ez, probably by Ethiopian Christians, at an uncertain date in the first millennium.

1 Meqabyan tells of a proud king, Tseerutsaydan, who worships seventy idols and forces his subjects to sacrifice to them, and of Maqabis of the tribe of Benjamin and his sons, who refuse and die as martyrs, then appear to the king in glory. Around this story the book gathers long sermons on God’s judgment, the resurrection of the dead, the fallen angels, and Israel’s history.

Read it as you would the life of a martyr: the history is loose, but the message is constant: God alone is to be worshipped, and those who suffer for him will rise again. The Catholic Church does not count it among the books of the Bible.
